nodes.label: Spec 0004 rationale: decision history of the schemas free of sample names spec (context, options considered, rationale)

Force: the localization schema requires a key named greeting_recipient; a catalog without it fails with 'en.json: data must contain ['greeting_recipient'] properties', yet the key belongs to the sample screen, not to every product

Force: the token schema requires a typography role named greeting; a token set without it fails with 'tokens: data.typography.semantic must contain ['greeting'] properties', and the name ties the large text style to one screen

Force: a product may not edit either schema without leaving the merge path; spec 0003 gives design-system/schemas/, shared/specifications/, scripts/ and tooling/ to the foundation, while token values, catalogs and app sources are shared and merged by hand

Force: the generator tests read shared files from a foundation owned path: test_generation.py loads the checkout's tokens in three tests and copies design-system/ and shared/ in a fourth; in a scratch clone at 7b6ca4f with the catalog key replaced, test_stale_edited_and_missing_files errors

Force: the role name is a contract between both apps: the generator turns it into FoundationTokens.typographyGreeting in Swift and Kotlin, read by GreetingScreen.swift, FoundationTheme.kt and GreetingTest.kt, and the token conventions ask that a consumed role is renamed with every reader in the same change
Force: spec 0003 fixes which names stay (FoundationTokens, FoundationTheme, foundation_strings.xml, shared/config/foundation.json); a property inside FoundationTokens is not on that list
Force: the other required names describe a use: eleven color roles, body, page, content, surface and feedback; none of them names a screen
Force: an empty catalog has no reader; both apps expect a string resource file with content, and the generator has always refused a catalog without the one required key
Force: one maintainer, and real caller first; a product that removes the sample is that caller and does not exist yet, so the proof has to run on a copy
Without a decision, the first product that replaces the greeting edits two schemas and one test file that the foundation owns, and every later foundation release conflicts on those files

Option 1 (chosen): fix the two schemas in place, rename the role to heading, give the generator tests their own source tree; pros: a product edits only shared paths, --test passes in every product, the generator is untouched; cons: seven fixture files, only --check covers checkout tokens, no alias

Option 2 (rejected): fix the schemas and rename the role, keep the tests on the checkout's sources and make them generic; no fixture files to keep, but the tests still depend on product content, assert less, and nothing proves a catalog without the sample key

Option 3 (rejected): require no typography role at all, only at least one role of any name; no later rename can break a product, but FoundationTheme.kt and the iOS screen need a role to read, it goes further than the scope row asks, and typography alone would follow a different rule

Reason: the ownership split of spec 0003 settles it; a foundation owned file that names shared content breaks once a product does what the foundation invites, true of the two schema lines and of the tests, so Option 2 leaves the same coupling in test_generation.py

Reason: Option 3 solves the rename for good but gives up a check the native code relies on; a required role is the one place where a missing role is reported next to its cause, and the scope row asks for a better name, not for fewer rules

The design was run in a scratch clone before the spec was written: Option 1 rewrote one line in each generated token file, --check passed, nine tests passed under Python 3.9.6, the welcome_title catalog passed, emptied sources failed --check but passed --test, and init-project.sh --test passed

The calls inside the chosen option were made in a coordinated run where the recommended option is taken and recorded; each call names its runner up, and a call marked heavy is costly to reverse once it is built

Recommendation (heavy): the role is named heading, for where the text is used, not a platform style; title was the runner up (on Android it would sit in headlineLarge while Material has a smaller titleLarge); headline was rejected because it is already the name of the primitive scale
Recommendation: the role stays required; the schema keeps heading and body as required typography roles (runner up: dropping the requirement, Option 3)

Recommendation: no alias for the old name; greeting is renamed in one change across three readers and a stale reader gets a compile error (runner up: keeping greeting as a second role for one release, which would leave the sample name in every product's generated API)

Recommendation: at least one key is written as minProperties: 1, a standard Draft 7 keyword the pinned validator already supports, with a refusal that names the file (runner up: allowing an empty catalog; other candidate: a test in generator code)

Recommendation: greeting_recipient stays in the sample; the scope row asks that the schema stop naming it, not that the sample change, and a rename would touch seven files for no gain (runner up: a neutral key such as recipient_name)

Recommendation: the tests read a fixture tree of files that mirrors the layout the generator reads, a readable example of the smallest valid source set (runner up: the same data as Python literals inside the test module)

Recommendation: the fixture differs from the checkout's sources on purpose (key welcome_title, weight bold, sizes 30 and 36), so a test that reads the wrong tree fails (runner up: a byte for byte copy of the checkout's token files)

Recommendation: the proof has two parts: a unit test that generates and checks the fixture on every push, and a scratch clone step with the real script once during verification (runner up: a --root flag on the generator with committed expected outputs)

Recommendation: only the two sample names change; the other sixteen required role names describe a use and stay, and the scale names headline and reading stay as a separate coupling listed as a Follow-up
Recommendation: the generator code is left alone; the property name already comes from the role name, so the rename needs no code change
Recommendation: no verify.md from this spec; /develop writes it from the Verification matrix in index.md, as it did for spec 0003
Recommendation: no References section; every decision rests on the repository itself

Cross check by a second model: it confirmed the file list, message texts and fixture, and found that the scratch clone steps would have tested uncommitted work, one expected result assumed a clean checkout, and the test module names were left open; all findings are applied in index.md

How this spec sits beside spec 0003: it changes no kept name and no owner, makes the ownership table true in practice (a product can replace the sample without editing a foundation owned path), and ticks the spec 0003 Follow-up line in the same change
